conflicts.point: Whether pre-training licenses for compute clusters exceeding 10^26 FLOPs serve as a necessary safeguard against catastrophic systemic risks or merely function as a regulatory moat that protects incumbent firms.

positions.stance: Mandatory pre-training audits are necessary because unvetted frontier models introduce irreversible civilizational risks that outweigh potential innovation delays.
Compute thresholds and licensing gates impose severe human costs by delaying life-saving technologies and entrenching legacy tech monopolies.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-training licenses for compute clusters exceeding 10^26 operations serve as a necessary safeguard against catastrophic risks or function as a regulatory moat.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position provides concrete economic mechanisms, detailing how fixed legal overhead and specialized compliance costs burden smaller developers. The safetyist position relies on abstract catastrophic risks without quantifying the probability of such failures relative to the certainty of market consolidation.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical demonstration that compliance costs represent a negligible fraction of total R&D budgets for open-source developers would reverse this evaluation.
